parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain two reasons why a business may conduct variance analysis.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: State how to calculate a fixed overhead capacity variance.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Prepare the flexible budget statement for the month of August.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Prepare a statement reconciling the flexible budget profit in (c) with the actual profit.

Additional information
The actual labour hour rate in August was $15.50.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
Explain the likely reasons for the favourable direct labour variance of $1980 with reference to
the analysis of its two sub-variances.

Additional information
The directors are aware of an upward trend in the direct material price. To keep the current profit
level, they have two options.
Option 1 Modify the existing product so that it requires less direct material.
Option 2 Reduce the advertising cost by one-third.

parts.label: (f)
parts.text: Advise the directors which option they should choose. Justify your answer.

Additional information
The directors adopt the NPV method for this investment appraisal and are about to make the
decision to buy the machine. The sales manager, however, thinks that the annual estimated sales
revenue may be only $380 000. All other information will remain the same.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Discuss whether the directors should be concerned about the uncertainty over the estimated
sales revenue. Support your answer with calculations.

Additional information
The directors are preparing the cash budget for Year 4. They have two options available for an
amount of $80 000.
Option 1 Continue to manufacture Product A for two more years by launching a promotional
campaign. (Despite the machine being fully depreciated, it can continue to be used for
two more years.)
Option 2 Start designing a new product, Product B, to be launched in Year 5.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Advise the directors which option they should choose. Justify your answer.
